actions.justification: Mandatory first action: establish baseline vital signs to identify the clinical syndrome and guide further workup for this patient with liver failure.
Assess the chief complaint to identify the presenting condition and direct appropriate guideline-based management.
Evaluate general status including mental status and overall clinical appearance, especially important given underlying liver failure which can present with encephalopathy or coagulopathy.

Patient with liver failure is at risk for hepatic encephalopathy. Assessing mental status is critical to identify altered consciousness, asterixis, or confusion that would indicate encephalopathy and guide management urgency.

In a patient with liver failure, abdominal assessment is essential to evaluate for ascites, hepatosplenomegaly, tenderness suggesting spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP), or signs of portal hypertension complications.
Cardiovascular assessment is needed to evaluate for circulatory dysfunction common in liver failure (hyperdynamic circulation, volume status), which will guide fluid management and further workup.

Patient has liver failure comorbidity, which can lead to hepatic encephalopathy. Neurological assessment is critical to identify any altered mental status or encephalopathy beyond basic mental status check already completed.
Liver failure patients are at risk for fluid imbalances, ascites, and dehydration. Assessing hydration status is important for guiding fluid management.
Liver failure patients are immunocompromised and at high risk for infections such as spontaneous bacterial peritonitis (SBP). Assessing for infection source is a priority in this phase.
Comprehensive patient assessment to integrate all findings gathered so far and identify the clinical syndrome, especially given liver failure comorbidity which may complicate presentation.
Patient has liver failure comorbidity; assessing for multi-organ dysfunction is critical to determine severity and guide management decisions.
Pain assessment has not been completed yet and is important for identifying the chief complaint severity and guiding further workup.
Patient with liver failure may have hepatopulmonary syndrome, pleural effusions, or ascites affecting respiratory mechanics. Respiratory assessment is important for complete workup.
Liver failure patients are at high risk for hepatorenal syndrome. Monitoring urine output is essential to detect early renal compromise.
Liver failure commonly presents with jaundice, spider angiomata, palmar erythema, and peripheral edema. Skin assessment helps gauge severity of hepatic dysfunction.

Assess neurological status more specifically with NIHSS to evaluate for stroke or other neurological conditions in a patient with liver failure, which can cause hepatic encephalopathy mimicking neurological deficits.
Assess musculoskeletal status to complete the physical examination, as liver failure patients can have muscle wasting, asterixis, and other musculoskeletal findings.
Hepatorenal syndrome is a serious complication of liver failure; checking baseline eGFR helps assess renal function and guides further management.

Patient with liver failure requires IV access for potential medication administration, fluid management, and lab draws. This is a foundational step in managing any patient with significant comorbidities.
Patient with liver failure warrants hepatology or gastroenterology specialist consultation to guide management, assess severity, and plan further workup.
Patient with liver failure at 90 minutes into evaluation requires hospital admission for monitoring, further diagnostic workup, and specialist-guided management.
